h.strategy: Favor hypotheses driven by strong structural mechanisms: (1) an edit matters less when the part it modifies is disconnected, bypassed, or redundant in the parent; (2) diminishing returns: adding capacity helps less when the parent already has plenty, and removing it hurts more when the parent has little; (3) bottlenecks: improving a component helps more when it is the sole path or limiting factor. Prefer conditions that change the edit's effect by a large amount over subtle ones. Avoid hypotheses whose direction depends on fine balances between competing effects. State each hypothesis's mechanism in one sentence.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 4 carries nothing.
With node 1 starved of input, edge 2 is dead so upgrading it is irrelevant.
With edge 5 absent node 2 cannot reach the output, so edge 1 is bypassed.
Node 2 becomes a dead end, so improving edge 2 has no effect on the output.
Edge 4 is already dead without node 1 input, so removing it costs nothing.
Edge 1 is already dead when node 2 cannot reach the output, so removing it costs nothing.
Edge 4 carries nothing when node 1 has no input.
Edge 1 is bypassed when node 2 cannot reach the output.
Adding a conv on a previously empty direct edge adds the most new capacity.
Adding a conv where the edge was empty adds more capacity than replacing an existing op.
